software: Crest Performance development surface redesign, based on v0.4.0
method: Step-by-step native app captures during real mouse and keyboard actions. Intermediate keyboard positions retained; captured states held for caption reading. No generated UI or LED animation. Silent; not real-time footage or latency evidence.

steps.caption: Play: each pad plays one note. Dots are decoded firmware lights; numbered rings identify virtual fingers.
Enable Latch. Click column 4, row 2; press A and K. Three fingers stay held independently.
Select finger 1, then press Right five times. Only its X position changes; the other fingers remain held.
Select finger 2, then press Up three times. Its Y movement controls timbre independently.
Select finger 3, then press [ five times. Pressure changes without moving the other fingers.
Release all removes every held contact. All three notes end; the stock note lights return.

Chords: the left hand uses compact control rows, grouped like Crest Flower. The right hand plays one I–VII bank across seven octave rows. One dark column separates the hands; extra outer pads are unused.
Enable Latch, then press I in octave 4 with the right hand: C4–E4–G4. A numbered ring marks the held contact; firmware supplies the light underneath.
Press Right twice and ] once while the finger is selected. X movement bends its three voices; the pressure key changes their pressure. These keys move the virtual contact before firmware processing.
Release all, then press I one row lower: C3–E3–G3. Playing rows change octave. With C selected and register zero, root octaves run from C0 at the bottom to C6 at the top.
Press II in C major: D4–F4–A4. Diatonic mode derives each quality from the selected scale. Keep the right hand on this bank while the left changes the nearby controls.
Press Inv+ in the second control row. Inversion becomes 1. Inv−, Inv0, Inv+ and Lead are adjacent, following Crest Flower’s voicing group. Controls change future attacks without sounding notes.
Press Spread at the end of the same row. Green means enabled: the second voiced tone moves up one octave. Oct−, Oct0 and Oct+ beside it change chord register.
Press Add9 directly above Spread. The top row groups Dim, Min, Maj, Sus4, 6, m7, Maj7 and Add9. Add9 adds the ninth without a seventh; 9 in the third row includes both.
Press I again: E4–C5–D5–G5, MIDI 64, 72, 74, 79. Inversion, spread and Add9 combine. Hover help lists the resulting pitches.
Release all. Press Inv0, Spread and Triad to restore root position, close spacing and a three-note chord. These controls are adjacent within the left-hand block.
Press Chrom in the third control row. Chromatic mode uses the same scale-degree roots with an explicit quality; Major is selected initially. Diat sits immediately to its left.
Press II: D4–F♯4–A4. Chromatic Major produces D major where Diatonic produced D minor. Degree and octave positions stay in the same bank.

Press Min and Maj7 on the same top row. Quality and extension are separate: this selects a minor-major seventh chord. Extensions remain exclusive in this library; the Flower grouping does not change that behavior.
Press I: C4–E♭4–G4–B4. Four output voices follow the selected quality and seventh. This demonstration captures MIDI; sound belongs to the downstream instrument.
Choose D in the Root selector above the instrument. Root and scale stay in the application UI. The chord-pad labels update without using any performance pads for key selection.
Focus the surface, then press K for I in octave 4: D4–F4–A4–C♯5. The keyboard contact follows the new D root. A contact on the dark separator is silent.
Release all leaves zero contacts and active notes. Default keys A–J trigger I–VII in octave 3; K triggers I in octave 4. Custom keyboard coordinate maps retain their physical assignments.

Strumplate keeps the same compact left-hand controls. The top of the right-hand bank selects I–VII; pads below pick individual tones. Automatic articulation pads are dark because manual presses determine timing.
Press V in the top row of the playing bank. This selects G harmony without sounding a chord. Picking pads now contain G, B and D in different octaves.
Press G4. One contact produces one note. Latch keeps it held while the next manual pick is added. Its numbered ring is separate from the firmware light.
Press B4 beside G4. Both notes stay held, with independent contact and expression ownership. In-cell X, Y and pressure affect only the selected finger’s note.
Press D5 to complete G4–B4–D5. The separate presses determine attack order and timing. Voicing and extension controls remain together under the left hand.
Select I at the top while G4, B4 and D5 remain held. Existing notes retain their pitches. Picking labels now describe C harmony for future presses.
Press C5 in the newly selected harmony. It joins the three old notes. Changing harmony did not retune held notes or transfer their expression ownership.
Release all clears every held note and control contact. Chords returns to full chord triggers; Play returns to ordinary firmware MPE playing.
Clips: the bundled performance-showcase session is loaded. Blue bottom-row pads 1–3 contain stopped phrases; the other slots are empty.
Latch is enabled for this demonstration. Press bottom-row pad 1: its green firmware light shows clip 1 looping.
Release all removes the launch contact. The clip continues: launch is a press action, not a hold.
Press and latch the pad directly above clip 1. Cyan marks mute; the loop continues while its notes are silenced.
Release all ends the mute hold. Green returns and future notes play at the continuing loop position.
Press row 4 above clip 1. Magenta shows octave-up held: future attacks shift up 12 semitones. Stored notes and held voices keep their pitches.
Release the octave hold. Blue returns; subsequent attacks use the original pitch.
Hold Fill: column 1, row 6. Magenta means Fill-conditioned attacks are enabled until the contact is released.
Release Fill. Yellow means ready. Fill changes conditions at future attacks; existing note releases remain valid.
Select Play and press A. The clip keeps looping while the new live finger has independent expression.
Return to Clips, then press pad 1 again. Blue confirms stopped; the captured phrase remains in its slot.

chord_layout_reference.adaptation: Contiguous quality/extension and voicing groups. LinnStrument retains left-hand controls beside a single right-hand degree bank. Existing chord register/spread controls replace Flower bass controls; musical modifier behavior is unchanged.
